**Observation Log:**

- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/04/11 (Tue) 01:56
- [USER] Part 29 discusses the Tribunal's consideration of material issues and the conclusion of an agreement between parties based on correspondence.
- [USER] The Tribunal dealt with the 19 July 2017 letter as part of a course of conduct leading to its conclusion.
- [USER] The builder did not cite Butler v Fairclough in post-hearing submissions but cited Haller, which the Tribunal referenced.
- [USER] Ground 6 concerns whether the Tribunal erred in finding the completion date of the works was 20 October 2010.
- [USER] Ground 7 questions whether leave to appeal should be granted based on the Tribunal's finding being against the weight of evidence.
- [USER] The Tribunal stated that practical completion occurred on 20 October 2010 when the FOC was issued.
- [USER] The definition of "building works" in the contract includes completion and handover to the owner in accordance with the contract documents.
- [USER] Clause 7.1 of the contract states that the builder must obtain and pay for all planning and building approvals.
- [USER] The FOC is a planning and building approval that allows lawful occupation based on conformity with preceding approvals.
- [USER] The Tribunal's reasoning indicates that physical works are of no use to the owner without legal approval for occupation.
- [USER] The definition of "practical completion" focuses on completeness except for matters not preventing usual use.
- [USER] The second emphasized words in the definition of "building works" may cover the written variation to the original contract.
- [USER] Part 30 discusses the argument regarding the practical completion date and the interpretation of "completion" under the contract.
- [USER] The builder's obligations under the contract were not complete until the owners received the FOC.
- [USER] The Tribunal's reasoning process regarding completion date includes the builder's responsibility for obtaining the FOC.
- [USER] The Tribunal's finding that completion occurred upon receipt of the FOC is contested.
- [USER] The Tribunal erred in interpreting relevant terms of the contract regarding the completion date.
- [USER] Clause 1 of the contract defines "building works" and "practical completion."
- [USER] Clause 7.1 names the builder as responsible for obtaining building and planning approvals.
- [USER] Clause 26.2(c) states that the final progress claim is to be made on practical completion and must include a certificate of occupancy if required.
- [USER] Clause 26.7 states that final payment to the builder is to be made within 5 working days after practical completion and receipt of relevant documentation.
- [USER] The Tribunal's finding that the FOC is part of the definition of "building works" is disputed.
